validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed. The Dauletabad–Sarakhs–Khangiran pipeline (aka Dauletabad–Salyp Yar) is the SECOND Turkmenistan→Iran gas import line, gas first flowed 3 Jan 2010, inaugurated in a ceremony 6 Jan 2010. Independent contemporaneous coverage (BBC News 6 Jan 2010; RFE/RL; Press TV; Fars) plus later analysis (Eurasian Research Institute) all describe the same physical line from Turkmenistan's Dauletabad gas field to Khangiran in NE Iran where it feeds the Iran Gas Trunkline (IGAT) system. Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correct — a gas transmission trunk (48-in / ~1,200 mm, ~182 km), not gathering/plant-internal, not oil/NGL. DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate. Distinct from P0749 Korpeje-Kordkuy (the FIRST, western Turkmenistan→Iran line into Golestan). GulfPub lists a separate 'Dauletabad - Sarakhs Loop' (16-in, ~76 km, NIOC) which is a smaller domestic loop connecting this line to the Sarakhs–Mashhad–Neka trunk — a different physical pipe, not this 48-in main; no GEM ProjectID collision found in the 31-row Iran gas operating roster. SPECS confirmed: Length 182 km corroborated by Wikipedia and ERI (GulfPub's '113' is the 113-MILE figure mislabeled as km, = 182 km, so it AGREES not conflicts). Diameter 48 in corroborated by GulfPub (dia=48). Capacity 12.5 bcm/y corroborated by ERI ('12,5 bcm' annually), consistent with Wikipedia's 'initially 6 bcm, up to 12 bcm'. Owner Turkmengaz + Iran Ministry of Petroleum reasonable (Turkmen section built/owned by Turkmengaz; Iran section NIOC/NIGC); existing owner ref (mfa.gov.tm) returns 200.

validity.recommendation: Change StartMonth1 from 10 to 01 (or clear it). The line was inaugurated 6 January 2010 (gas began 3 Jan 2010), not October 2010.
validity.researcher_notes: DATE ERROR. The sheet records StartYear1=2010, StartMonth1=10 (i.e. October 2010). Every independent source dates the start to early January 2010: BBC News (6 January 2010, 'Turkmenistan opens new Iran gas pipeline'), RFE/RL (6 Jan 2010), Press TV/Fars (6 Jan 2010), and Wikipedia ('gas began pumping on 3 January 2010... inaugurated 6 January 2010'). Year (2010) is correct; the month value 10 is wrong and should be 01. Likely a transcription slip (10 vs 01).

validity.researcher_notes: PROVINCE ERRORS. (1) The Dauletabad (Döwletabat) gas field is in MARY Province, Turkmenistan (Wikipedia 'Dauletabad gas field': 'located in Mary, Mary province, Turkmenistan'; part of Amu-Darya province, ~36.6°N 61.3°E). The sheet's StartState/Province='Ahal Province' is wrong — probably confused with a similarly-named Dovletabat suburb near Ashgabat in Ahal Province. (2) EndState/Province='Khorasan Khorasan Province' is a duplicated-word typo; Khangiran / Shahid Hasheminejad Gas Refinery near Sarakhs is in RAZAVI KHORASAN Province, Iran (Wikipedia 'Khangiran gas refinery'). FuelSource='Dauletabad gas field' is correct. Endpoints Dauletabad→Khangiran are correct as named places, but the route-tab start/end read 'Asia'→'Asia' (placeholder) and should carry the named facilities.

Natural gas line; unambiguous across all sources.
Long-haul cross-border transmission trunk feeding the IGAT system at Khangiran; not gathering/distribution.
Sourced from the Dauletabad (Döwletabat) gas field, Mary Province, Turkmenistan — the field the pipeline is named for.

routes.end_name: Shahid Hasheminejad (Khangiran) Gas Refinery, near Sarakhs, Razavi Khorasan, Iran
routes.corridor_desc: Runs ~182 km from the Dauletabad gas field in southeastern Mary Province, Turkmenistan, southwest to the Sarakhs area where it crosses the Iran–Turkmenistan border (final ~30.5 km to Sarakhs per Wikipedia), then ~35 km on to the Shahid Hasheminejad (Khangiran) Gas Refinery in the Khangiran area of Sarakhs county, Razavi Khorasan, Iran, where it ties into the IGAT trunkline system. Corridor is tightly bounded (short, single well-known field-to-refinery route); endpoint coordinates are sourced (Khangiran refinery from Wikipedia) or defensible approximations (Dauletabad field ~36.6°N 61.3°E from Wikidata Q2033768 — the Wikipedia field article notes no explicit coords, so treated as approximate).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named facilities: Dauletabad field (start) and Shahid Hasheminejad/Khangiran refinery (end), with Sarakhs as the border waypoint (well-known town, ~36.545°N 61.158°E). Khangiran refinery coord 36.468°N 60.849°E is sourced from Wikipedia. Dauletabad field coord ~36.605°N 61.32°E is a defensible approximation (Wikidata); flagged approximate, not fabricated. Existing route already high-accuracy (QGIS-mapped 8/29/24) — no re-derivation needed; this confirms named endpoints and corrects the placeholder 'Asia'→'Asia' start/end labels.
